text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Government-monitored prices of basic goods rose 13.8 percent in the first half of September, National Statistics Institute officials said.
-- British consultancy KPMG will help Bulgaria's troubled national carrier Balkan Airlines to work out a programme aimed at stabilising its finances, transport ministry officials said.

-- Bulgaria's National Electricity Company experts and Energy Ministry officials are expected to leave for Moscow today for talks with Russia's atomic energy ministry officials on funding the reconstruction of four Soviet-made reactors at Bulgaria's Kozloduy nuclear power plant.

-- Bulgaria's private Capitalbank decided to raise capital to 1.4 billion levs by March 31, 1997 to meet new higher minimum capital requirements set by the central bank, the bank's board chairman said.
-- Bulgaria's state fund Zemedelie is expected to seal contracts with four banks today for extending loans worth 16 billion levs for the autumn sowing, the fund's executive director said.
-- The Dutch ING bank is expected to extend $4.0 million loan to Bulgaria's National Electricity Company (NEC) within two days, NEC officials said.

-- Bulgaria's central bank rejected the idea to allow Bulgaria's second largest credit institution, the State Savings Bank (SSB), to collect deposits in foreign currency because this would harm commercial banks, the newspaper said without quoting sources.
The SSB, which holds the bulk of Bulgarians' lev savings and provides 100 percent guarantee on them, is governed by a special law which bans it from collecting foreign currency deposits.
-- Bulgaria's inflation for 1996 will hit 700 percent if the funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund fails, a former economic advisor to premier Zhan Videnov said.

-- Bulgaria's sports lottery operator and Greece's Intracom group said they had sealed a deal to introduce modern technology into the Bulgarian game, ending a long-running battle between the two firms.
-- Bulgaria's state-owned Bulbank and the State Savings Bank and appeared on The Banker magazine's rating list of best 500 European banks, ranking 248th and 398th respectively.
-- Bulgaria's Bank Consolidation Company and the central bank are preparing rehabilitation programme for restructuring of the banking sector, which is expected to be ready by September 18.

-- Bulgaria needs $620 million by the end of this year that can be raised only through the sale of big state-owned companies, Prime minister Zhan Videnov told ministers, deputies and regional governors on Sunday night. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
